talks.text: Who spends the most money on war? From nearly one trillion dollars... to absolutely nothing. 197 countries, one by one: the military budget, and how much of the economy it eats.
Grey: no army, or no data.
Green: up to one hundred billion.
And purple... over one hundred billion dollars! Let's go!
United States: $954 billion. 3.1% of GDP. Number one, by far!
954 billion dollars. More than the next six countries combined.
Ireland: $1.6 billion. 0.2% of GDP. One of the lowest shares in Europe.
Germany: $114 billion. 2.3% of GDP. Number four!
114 billion euros... sorry, dollars. Germany is back.
Four and a half percent. The most in NATO!
Greece: $8.4 billion. 3% of GDP. Almost three percent!
Almost forty percent of our whole economy. We have no choice.
Russia: $190 billion. 7.5% of GDP. Number three.
190 billion. Seven and a half percent of everything we make.
Venezuela: $2.1 billion. 2.2% of GDP. Last official figure: 2017.
Zero. We abolished our army in 1948.
Cuba: $130 million. 2.9% of GDP. Last official figure: 2018.
Haiti: $39 million. 0.1% of GDP. Almost nothing.
Trinidad and Tobago: $230 million. 0.9% of GDP.
Saint Kitts and Nevis: no data!
Nearly eight percent of our economy.
83 billion dollars. For a country of 37 million.
Oman: $6 billion. 5.7% of GDP. One of the highest shares on Earth.
United Arab Emirates: $23 billion. 5.6% of GDP. Last official figure: 2014.
Myanmar: $5 billion. 6.6% of GDP. Nearly seven percent!
China: $336 billion. 1.7% of GDP. Number two.
Papua New Guinea: $110 million. 0.3% of GDP.
Algeria: $25 billion. 8.8% of GDP. The highest share in Africa!
Eritrea: $180 million. 20.9% of GDP. Last official number: 2003!
Republic of the Congo: $200 million. 1.3% of GDP.
Central African Republic: $74 million. 2.3% of GDP.
Should your country spend more, or less? Comment below!
